<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)

- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ae89e67d7e76c7b765f6b1a7d517754d906bbe3f && git checkout ae89e67d7e76c7b765f6b1a7d517754d906bbe3f

git fetch origin 4fe3af9d7e9cb59d63b0a69217197b000fb34b2b 5a3e45078e45624641d5fded12beac4ff612c5dd && git checkout -B drift-repro 4fe3af9d7e9cb59d63b0a69217197b000fb34b2b && git merge --no-ff 5a3e45078e45624641d5fded12beac4ff612c5dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fe3af9d7e9cb59d63b0a69217197b000fb34b2b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4fe3af9d7e9cb59d63b0a69217197b000fb34b2b` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a3e45078e45624641d5fded12beac4ff612c5dd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts, packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts (CliExitCode, emitJson, isExitSignal), packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-exit.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts (refuseWhenHostConfigUnloadable), every command module under packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/ (the 15 roster members and the 4 non-members account-issuer, duplicates, plan, unmapped-columns, plus index.ts), packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts, packages/cli/tsconfig.test.json, packages/cli/package.json, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.reads-env-files.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/exit-signal.pin.test.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json, skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md, content/docs/upgrading.mdx, content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .github/workflows/docs-drift-check.yml. Prose face judged in ②: .changeset/24949-migrate-apply-confirmation-exit.md.

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff against main (merge-base `e4d604efd3`; `origin/main` at `4fe3af9d7e` is 5 commits past it, none under packages/cli; the two-dot and three-dot diffs of the three paths are byte-identical): 3 files, +434 / -1. One code hunk, apply.ts:615-628.

1. **Accept-set change, right.** In `os migrate apply`, when `!flags.yes` and (`flags.json` or `!process.stdin.isTTY`) and `totalIntended > 0`, after every refusal above the gate: the text face now runs `printWarning(...)` then `this.exit(1)` (was `return`, exit 0); the `--json` face emits the same document with `emitJson(doc, 1)` (was 0), which sets `process.exitCode = 1` after draining the write (format.ts:114-120, 304-310) and `run()`'s `exitOneShotCommand(process.exitCode)` (apply.ts:139-153) leaves with it. `refuseWhenHostConfigUnloadable` between them is a no-op on this path (it returns false when the host config loaded, and the unloadable case already returned at apply.ts:401-416 above the gate). The warning line and the document (`message: 'confirmation_required'`, `hint: 'pass --yes'`, `applied: []`, `skipped: drift`, `pending`) are byte-unchanged. The thrown ExitError is rethrown by the enclosing catch (`isExitSignal`, apply.ts:721-724) so no second report, and `finally` still runs `stack.shutdown()`.

2. **Which runs now exit 1 that exited 0 before — the complete set, four runs.** (a) `apply --allow-destructive`, stdin not a TTY, no `--yes`, text face; (b) the same under `--json`; (c) plain `apply` on safe / needs_confirm drift or pending additive work, stdin not a TTY, no `--yes`, text face; (d) the same under `--json`. Nothing else can reach the hunk: it is guarded by `!flags.yes`, by the non-interactive test, and by `totalIntended > 0`.

3. **No run that should succeed is refused.** Verified unchanged in the cited code: `--yes` skips the gate entirely (apply.ts:623); an interactive `y` proceeds through `confirm()` (apply.ts:633); an interactive `n` keeps `printInfo('Aborted — no changes made.'); return;` and leaves through the one-shot exit with code 0 (apply.ts:634) — the pin's control case asserts exactly this (one prompt, no write, exit 0); a database with nothing to apply returns at the in-sync branch (apply.ts:297-335) or the `nothing_safe_to_apply` branch (apply.ts:608-612), both exit 0 and both ABOVE the gate; `--json --yes` is untouched; the PARTIAL exit 1 after a confirmed apply is untouched. The `[#13118]` unloadable-host-config refusal, the issuer pre-flight, the reactions and organization-ownership refusals all sit above the gate and are unchanged.

4. **Interactive decline unchanged — yes.** apply.ts:634 is not in the diff; the pin's "terminal answered n" control holds it at exit 0 with no write.

5. **"Non-interactive" detection is one rule across the family, right.** Every gate in the tree reads `flags.json || !process.stdin.isTTY` (16 sites: apply.ts:624, activity-changed-fields.ts:120, audit-mail-bodies.ts:231, audit-metadata-bodies.ts:125, comment-parent-pair.ts:122, comment-reactions.ts:146, files-to-references.ts:204, meta.ts:1450, multi-value-columns.ts:401, recorded-by.ts:185, resume.ts:222, security-catalog-overlays.ts:205, summary-nulls.ts:167, value-shapes.ts:120; organization-ownership.ts:684-693 reads `!json && confirm()`), and each member's private `confirm()` returns false on `!process.stdin.isTTY` before building readline. No CI variable is read anywhere. The siblings' spelling is `emitJson({ error: 'confirmation_required', hint: 'pass --yes' }, 0); this.exit(1)` and `printWarning(...); this.exit(1)` (comment-reactions.ts:146-155 read verbatim); apply's `emitJson(..., 1); return` reaches the same status by its own existing refusal spelling (apply.ts:177-185 and 581-596 use it). Family exit is now one code.

6. **Public surface.** `CliExitCode` is `0 | 1` (format.ts:54), unchanged; no helper, constant, flag, document key or export is added. Not inventing a shared helper is right: 14 sites already inline the exit and a helper would be a refactor outside the card. apply's `--json` document names the condition in `message` where the siblings use `error` — pre-existing, unchanged, a declared hold-off (`--json` documents beyond their exit).

7. **The pin's population discovers every apply-mode subcommand in the tree — yes, verified against the source.** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/` at the head holds 19 command modules plus index.ts (test files excluded by the pin's filter). Exactly 15 declare a boolean `yes` or `apply` flag — activity-changed-fields, apply, audit-mail-bodies, audit-metadata-bodies, comment-parent-pair, comment-reactions, files-to-references, meta, multi-value-columns, organization-ownership, recorded-by, resume, security-catalog-overlays, summary-nulls, value-shapes — and that is the ROSTER. The four non-members (account-issuer, duplicates, plan, unmapped-columns) and index.ts carry no `isTTY` test and no `confirm()`: they are read-only reports. Every confirmation gate in the tree sits in a module the discovery rule selects, so the roster is complete. Limit, noted and not a defect: `readdirSync` is non-recursive and the rule keys on the flag names `yes`/`apply`, so a future member escapes only by living in a sub-directory or by naming its confirmation flag something else — both outside the family's convention today, and the roster-equality case fails by id for every member the rule does see. The second family case (every member has a boolean `json` flag) is true per the tree.

8. **Per-member cases are sound.** Both faces per member with `process.stdin.isTTY` set false by the run itself; exit read from the ExitError's `oclif.exit`, else the mocked one-shot exit's code, else `process.exitCode`; the text face must contain the member's confirmation flag (`--yes`, or `--backup-taken` for organization-ownership); the write seams untouched (the boot for pre-boot gates; `flushSchemaDdl`/`applyMigrationEntries` for apply; the journal runners for recorded-by/resume); no prompt recorded. Replaced seams are the occupancy probe, the boot, the journal reads, the sentinel scan, the one-shot exit and readline; parse, gates, `emitJson` and `this.exit` run for real. Red-on-main (2 failed: apply text and json) and the three ablations (each exactly 1 failed, including the comment-reactions sibling row) are consistent with the diff's shape — the apply rows are the only ones the hunk can flip. The tier is unit: no value import of `bootSchemaStack` (vi.mock only), no spawn, no driver import — `vitest-tiers.ts` signals (lines 160-178) agree, and `tsconfig.test.json` includes `test/**/*` so `check:test-typecheck` compiles it.

9. **Nothing in-tree pins the old exit.** `plan.reads-env-files.integration.test.ts:171` reads apply's `message`, not its exit; `exit-signal.pin.test.ts:813/859` pin siblings at exit 1; the QA checklist `cli.json:260/301` pins the `--json` payload, not the status; no script, workflow, Dockerfile, example or published skill runs `os migrate apply` non-interactively without `--yes` (git grep at the head: every hit is prose). `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md:192-194` already tells agents the family refuses in a non-TTY "exiting 1 with confirmation_required" — this diff brings apply to that published contract. The break is external (deploy scripts reading `$?`) and is carried by the changeset.

10. **The `[#24949]` comment** matches apply.ts's existing convention (22 `[#NNNN]` comments at base); `check-doc-authoring` roots are `.claude`, `docs`, `skills`, `content`, not packages.

11. **Docs that still say "exits 0".** `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx:280-281` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails: never edited in a code PR; the changeset is the PR's input) — leaving it is right. `content/docs/upgrading.mdx:383-384` (Upgrading to 18.0, step 8) is a hand-written tree page; its sentence is framed as the measured 18.0.0 walk and stays true of 18.0.0, but reads as present-tense guidance and becomes false for the cli version that ships this change. Not a defect of the diff (no rule requires a docs rider; the docs-drift job is advisory and labelled the PR `documentation`), but see ③ for the carrier correction.

12. **Check-runs on the head, all completed at render time:** 40 names, 0 failed, 0 pending. Success: Build Core; Test Core and all six shards; Lint & Repo Gates; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · ESLint; Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped (query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus, tooling self-tests); TypeScript Type Check; Type Check · consumer gates / debt ledger / source gates / workspace; Check Changeset; Governed Surface Queue Guard; Dogfood Regression Gate; Flag docs affected by code changes; Check Documentation Links; Check PR Size; Auto Label; filter; the three claim/card guards. Skipped by opt-in or path filter, not failures: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Dogfood shards and Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance. Nothing on this head is NOT MEASURED.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/24949-migrate-apply-confirmation-exit.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': minor`. The diff publishes exactly one package source, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts (`@objectstack/cli` 18.0.0, not private); the test and the changeset publish nothing. One package, one bump — matches what the diff publishes.
- **Level right.** `(narrowing)` is BREAKING (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3), and during the launch window a breaking change ships `minor` (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header and line 1670: "a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`"). `major` would be refused by that guard; `patch` would understate a status that narrows. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- **BREAKING banner present** with the bang in the title line (`fix(cli)!:`), and the migration carried: FROM (nothing applied, exit 0) → TO (nothing applied, exit 1), the Unchanged list (interactive `n` still 0, `--yes` applies and exits 0, nothing-to-apply exits 0 without asking — each verified against apply.ts in ①), and the one-line fix (pass `--yes`, or run `os migrate plan`). Accurate to the code.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`** on the changeset (line 9) and the PR body (line 2). Right arm: nothing new is accepted — no key, flag, field or document shape — and a class of input the command admitted as success (a scripted run without `--yes`) is now refused by status. The narrowing face is what makes this CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER review owed before the queue; the Governed Surface Queue Guard is green because no governed path is in the file list.
- **ADR-0087 disposition right.** Exactly one marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. No spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored shape or exported declaration moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the remedy is a flag on the operator's command line, not a consumer-code rewrite. Mechanically consistent with the gate read at the head: the body carries no arrow rewrite, no migration-framed heading, no rewrite table and no FROM → TO label line (the `**FROM:**`/`**TO:**` bullets corroborate only when a label placeholder exists, and none does), so `findMigrationPrescription` returns null and the arm is not refused. The other four dispositions are closed in the marker on facts (published; no ids; no export narrowed). The "Lint · CI, release & engine gates" family is green on the head, and the dev's local run listed the changeset as `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

- **Dev flag — Zone 3 shared helper not taken.** Answered: right. `CliExitCode` is `0 | 1`, the 14 sibling sites inline `this.exit(1)` correctly, and the discovered-population pin holds the family to one code; a helper is a refactor beyond the card.
